When performing user behavior analysis, we usually need to clarify the object of analysis (i.e. subject), query and analyze its behavior data in a certain application. DataFinder provides you with multi\-application, multi\-agent, and multi\-ID type analysis capabilities. It supports creating multiple applications and multiple subjects in the DataFinder project, and supports setting multiple identification ID types for subjects to improve the flexibility of analysis. This article introduces an overview of DataFinder's multi\-application, and multi\-ID type analysis capabilities.

<span id="e18a8077"></span>
# Precautions


|Attention segmentation |Detailed description |
|---|---|
|Environmental constraints |SaaS\-cloud\-native and private environments are supported. |
|Function switch |This feature is for advanced use and is currently available on demand for customers with relatively complex business needs.<br><br><br>* Customers who newly purchased Finder after privatization version 4.4 can freely open it on demand, and the multi\-application function is turned on by default; the multi\-subject and multi\-ID type functions are turned off by default.<br><br>* A SaaS\-cloud native environment requires the purchase of CDP oneID configuration capabilities. Please consult BytePlus technical support for details. |
|Binding relationship |* A DataFinder project supports binding multiple applications.<br><br>* An application only supports the option to bind one principal.<br><br>* A principal can be bound by multiple applications.<br><br>   When a subject is bound by multiple applications, subsequent data analytics supports the analysis of the current subject's behavior data in multiple applications, and can also filter through the application ID to analyze only the subject's behavior data in some of the applications.<br><br><br><div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-tips-is-title="true">warning</div><br><br><br><div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning">Since an app only supports binding one principal, if you need to use the multi\-principal feature to perform data analytics on multiple agents, you need to create multiple apps in your project, each binding one principal.</div><br> |
|Other related products |When using the multi\-agent function, you also need to activate the CDP product at the same time. |


<span id="44b95003"></span>
# Basic concept


|Term |Concept note |
|---|---|
|Application |The basic carrier of data can directly correspond to an APP, web page, Mini Program, etc. |
|Subject |Data analytics objects, such as users, consumers, merchants, vehicles, etc., are used to describe who the event belongs to, that is, who triggered the behavior. |
|ID type |For the identification of the analysis object, for example, a natural person can be accurately identified by the ID number, but such accurate identification is too sensitive. Generally, a user needs to be approximately defined by IDs such as device ID, email address, mobile phone number, and registered account number. |


<span id="a7012d51"></span>
# Application scenario


|Feature Overview ||Application scenario example |
|---|---|---|
|Multi\-application |* For enterprises that operate multiple touchpoints/applications simultaneously, only single\-ended data can be seen at the DataFinder single\-application level, and the perspective of user analysis is relatively isolated and fragmented.<br><br>* After enabling multi\-application/multi\-agent/multi\-ID type functions, multiple applications can be aggregated in a single project, enabling summary statistics between multiple applications, identifying real user assets, and analyzing the user journey across the touchpoint lifecycle.<br><br>* Usually, when planning event tracking, each end uses the same set of event tracking design, but in the DataFinder single application perspective, metadata needs to be maintained independently, which introduces more extra work and the risk of errors. Once this capability is enabled, apps under the same project will share event tracking schemes, allowing for more elegant data management. |* Under the Douyin business system, the company needs to know the degree of user overlap between Douyin ontology and Douyin Lite, and whether the behavioral patterns are consistent, so as to determine whether a function needs to be differentiated and implemented.<br><br>* A DTC brand maintains multiple touchpoints online. Users at different stages such as cognition, interest, and first purchase need to reach through different touchpoint design content and activities. The user journey is becoming more and more complex. Marketers need to accurately measure marketing effects through cross\-touchpoint attribution capabilities to confirm subsequent marketing actions and budget allocations.<br><br>* A new power car company is making intelligent efforts, and has added the function of APP and large\-screen linkage through OTA capabilities. The team hopes to understand whether this ability has achieved the expected linkage effect and whether there are breakpoints in driver operation, so as to confirm the follow\-up iteration direction. |
|Multi\-agent and multi\-ID types |From the perspective of the data model, DataFinder currently defines the analysis object through the "user" model by default, and the ID system is relatively simple. For more complex business systems, it is often not enough to describe the current business state through a single user entity, and even errors may occur. |* In platform APPs such as e\-commerce, users often need to distinguish between two identities of merchants and consumers, each with an independent ID identifier. Previously, although it was possible to use different IDs to deduplicate the statistics of users through the historical analysis of the subject switching function, if there is a user who is both a merchant and a consumer, the attributes (such as credit rating) describing the user will be based on the latest value coverage, and the consumer's credit rating will be used to describe the merchant's error situation during business analysis.<br><br>* A bank has various business support systems for retail, corporate, and internal employees. There are different caliber IDs among the subjects of each business service, but their values may be the same. If a set of ID calibers is still used, it will lead to erroneous associations between the subjects. For example, if the job numbers of an employee and an operator of a business are both No. 1, if the main body and the caliber are not distinguished, the behavior of the two types of main bodies will be triggered by a "user" by default. |


<span id="f665587b"></span>
# Functional logic

After enabling DataFinder's multi\-application/multi\-agent/multi\-ID type function, multiple applications can be created in each project, and multiple analysis subjects and analysis caliber ID types can be set up. Through the ID\-MAPPING calculation of multi\-application data fusion and multi\-caliber, we can maximize the recovery of a consumer or a natural person, thus connecting the behavior of different subjects in multiple applications.

<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," />

Of which:


* After opening the multi\-application/multi\-subject/multi\-ID type function, when reporting subsequent data, you need to clearly mark which application/subject data is reported (by indicating the **appid** of the reported data), and which caliber ID type of the data is (indicate **user_unique_id_type** ).

* In some scenarios, we can obtain other ID types associated with the subject. In order to ensure the accuracy of the association relationship, when reporting data, it is recommended that you use the **id_bind** ability provided by DataFinder to report the binding relationship between the caliber and the caliber in real time. Through the **ID\-MAPPING** calculation under the multi\-caliber, the reported device information and user information are mapped, and finally the **ssid** provided by DataFinder is used to restore a consumer or natural person as accurately as possible.

   For example, the customer can get the mobile phone number phone_id in the login state, and can get the card number card_id after tying the card, and can get the relationship between phone_id and card_id when tying the card. Assuming that a user gets phone_id1 in the login state, phone_id1 bound to ssid1, then all events reported in phone_id1 will belong to ssid1, assuming that card_id1 can be obtained after tying the card, if directly reported in card_id1, since the id service has not received any relationship with card_id1, then a new ssid2 will be generated, and events reported with card_id1 will belong to ssid2. The behavior before and after using the card number cannot be correlated, which obviously does not meet expectations.

   Therefore, both the server level and the client side provide **id_bind** way to report the binding relationship in advance.

   Before using card_id1 to report, you should call id_bind, bind phone_id1 and card_id1, card_id1 will also bind to ssid1, and then use card_id1 to report events will belong to ssid1, and the behavior before and after using the card number can be accurately associated.

<span id="四、常见问题"></span>
# Common problem

<span id="61e049da"></span>
## Q1: What is the difference between a principal and an item (business object)?

The default subject of Finder is the user. The main scenario of introducing the item business object is to expand the properties of the item itself when the user operates an item. The subject itself has not changed and is still "human".

For multi\-agent, the most common scenario is to distinguish between "human" and "non\-human" scenarios, such as: people, cars, analyzing behavior with people as the main body, and analyzing the behavior of cars with cars as the main body. The core reason for using different subjects is that the ID system of the analysis subject is different, just like the car has a license plate number and the person does not have a license plate number; the person has an ID number, but the car does not have an ID number; in terms of functional versatility, we also support the determination of "driver" and "passenger", "doctor" and "patient" as different analysis subjects, because their ID systems are different, although they are all "people".

<span id="b3ca6b2e"></span>
## Q2: What is the difference between DataFinder's original analysis principal function and this multi\-principal function?

In addition to the concept of the data model level, the new subject is mainly used to quickly find all the application data associated with the subject in the analysis scenario, while the original analysis subject is only used to confirm which attribute is used to calculate the corresponding number of subjects for the standard deduplicate in the analysis. To avoid ambiguity, we have renamed the original "analysis subject" to "statistical caliber".
